author: Inside Edition
description: Inside Edition's Eva Pilgrim sat down with Alex Murdaugh's attorneys Dick Harpootlian and Jim Griffin after the South Carolina Supreme Court's decision to toss out Murdaugh's double murder conviction, finding that the court clerk, Becky Hill, had unfairly influenced the jury. Despite the new court ruling, Murdaugh will remain in prison where the disgraced lawyer is serving 40 years for stealing from his clients.
title: Could Alex Murdaugh Be Acquitted In A Retrial?

author: Inside Edition
description: A man was completely flabbergasted over the number of boxes in a shipment he received from Walmart. Each box contained one foam swimming noodle. There were 165 boxes delivered the first day and 75 the next day for a total of 240 boxes. 35-year-old Matthew Bright says the noodles are typically delivered with several of them in one box. Bright uses the noodles by cutting them up and using them as packing material. He restores antique cookware and shops the pots and pans back to the owners. Bright says Walmart is giving him a $50 gift card for his trouble and offered to pick up all the boxes.
title: Man Shocked By How Walmart Delivered His Swimming Noodles

author: Inside Edition
description: A family in a car had a terrifying brush with death. A plane made an emergency landing and hit the highway hard, coming close to a head-on crash. The plane's wings just barely cleared the car and the plane's propeller clipped the side. Kristal Ewing was in the car with her husband and two children returning home from a hike in Mesa, Arizona. Ewing spoke with Inside Edition's Alison Hall. Everyone in the car and the pilot walked away without any injuries.
title: Plane Caught On Camera Nearly Crashing Into Car During Emergency Landing On Highway

author: Inside Edition
description: Police in Parker, Colorado, came to the rescue when a skunk had a mishap with a frightening object: someone's litter. The call came in at 3 a.m., and Parker Police arrived with a catchpole in hand. But after assessing the situation, they decided to take a different approach. It looked easy, until you consider that skunks are known to have a foul-smelling, oily spray that can hit a target up to 10 to 15 feet away. Inside Edition Digital has more.
title: Colorado Police Rescue Skunk Stuck In A Cup

author: Inside Edition
description: Melissa Elicio, a nurse from Arizona, was one of the 17 trapped tourists. She documented the ordeal.
title: Tourists Got Trapped In Vegas Elevator For Almost An Hour #shorts

author: Inside Edition
description: The pig doth protest, but so did the neighbors who called 911 after seeing the animal wandering around their neighborhood. This is Hamlet and something was rotten in the state of Ohio as long as he was away from home. While he charmed the responding officers, they were still committed to reuniting him with his family. A neighbor, who believed he knew which house was the pig's, helped get him back there. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Pig Named Hamlet Returned Home By Cops After Escaping From Yard
